edition.title: Computer Organization and Architecture: Designing for Performance
edition.author: William Stallings
edition.note: The syllabus prescribes the 9th ed. The available copy is the 10th. Substance is equivalent for every mapped chapter; the NUMBERING is not.

chapters.title: Introduction
chapters.note: Only the opening sections. The rest of book ch.1 is the evolution material the syllabus puts in its chapter 2.

chapters.title: Computer Evolution and Performance
chapters.note: SPLIT ACROSS TWO BOOK CHAPTERS. Evolution (vacuum tubes to multicore, the x86 and ARM lines) is book ch.1 from 1.4 on; performance assessment (clock speed, MIPS, Amdahl, Little) is the whole of book ch.2. This is the single biggest structural difference between the editions.

chapters.title: Top Level View of Computer Function and Interconnection
Cache Memory
chapters.note: Includes Appendix 4A, Performance Characteristics of Two-Level Memories, which is where the hit-ratio and average-access-time maths lives.

chapters.title: Computer Arithmetic
chapters.note: Book ch.9 (Number Systems) does not exist in the 9th ed and is assumed knowledge here — the prerequisite is Microprocessors. It is listed because two's complement and floating-point representation are defined there, not in ch.10.

chapters.title: Instruction Sets: Addressing Modes and Format
Instruction Level Parallelism and Superscalar Parallelism
Multicore Computer
chapters.note: Book ch.17 (Parallel Processing) carries the multiprocessor organisation and cache-coherence material the syllabus lists under its chapter 17.

chapters.title: Distributed Systems Architecture
chapters.note: NOT IN THE BOOK, in either edition. Stallings ends at GPGPUs; there is no client-server, distributed-object or CORBA chapter. Its topics cell in the syllabus is also empty, so the four unit outcomes are the entire specification. The three open sources in docs/CPE412-CURRICULUM.md §4.1 are not a convenience here — they are the only material this chapter has.
